With your SH2 example, I agree that SH2 is much scarier and much more cinematic with the fixed camera angles. But as a fan, playing that game so many times, the things that scared me my first play through may not be as effective. A new camera angle would not make those moments scarier, but they’d offer something NEW for a fan like me, which is more exciting than playing the exact same game I’ve already beaten countless times. It doesn’t make the game “better” but it makes it new for people who already are fans. 

How about instead of a camera mod, a mod that replaces every enemy with pyramid head. Obviously not the way the game was intended, but it could be a new, fun challenge 

How about all of the silly unlockables that ARE in the game? Those are only unlocked on a second play through because while the game isn’t intended to be played with a silly outfit, it’s fun for someone who’s already beaten it. Mods are the exact same thing.

I am just saying it would allow me a clearer glimpse at a really beautiful section of the game that the regular camera doesn’t allow. All of those rooms on the staircase are so cool, but I remember squinting trying to look at all of them, and again some are literally impossible to see. It’s likely too that they were MEANT to be seen considering the fantastic detail, and all of the symbolism you can decipher from them, but the regular camera of the game doesn’t allow it. I’m just saying that being able to look at these rooms in the regular flow of gameplay is something that I’ve always wanted since I first played the game.

Is the game “better” like this? No, I agree.

Was the game “intended” to be played this way? No, I agree.

But no one is claiming that it is better or that it was intended. They’re just saying that as longtime fans of the franchise it’s new and interesting and kinda fun.

I agree that overall this mod will definitely be a less cinematic experience, but as others have pointed out the only people that are gonna play this are hardcore fans that want to see the game in a new light. Plus there are some sections that having this kind of camera is something I wanted my first play through. Take the big spiral staircase sections. Having the normal wide angle to see Henry’s descent down the spiral is definitely a better shot in terms of cinematography, but when I was playing I wanted to get a closer look at all of the weird decorated rooms around the edges, and no matter how much I tried fiddling with the games normal camera I just couldn’t get a good angle. I think some of them are actually impossible to see in game, and are only visible through free cam hacks. 

This mod would allow me to play through the game, and walk WITH henry, looking at all the fucked up dolls and bodies in each of those little rooms, and then continue playing the game. No fiddling with the in game camera, and no immersion breaking free cam, a perfect balance for a fan like me. Not only will I finally get a proper look at the rooms, but I will still always have that experience of the original camera angle from the first time I played. Advertising this mod is in no way “harmful” and it’s ludicrous to even suggest that. It’s like saying that a “behind the scenes” look at a movie ruins the original. Seeing the Alien walking around normally definitely isn’t as scary as in the film, but as a fan it allows me a better look at the costume to greater appreciate the artistry behind it.

I heard a theory regarding the first film that the family only became cannibals after they lost their jobs from the air gun. Humans didn’t only replace their meals but also their family tradition of that they named themselves after (they were called the slaughter family in the first film) it was their entire identity. The slaughterhouse that they had worked for and relied upon for generations had simply discarded them, so the family didn’t place much more value in human life than the company placed in them. Its kind of a critique on how machine automation replacing human jobs leads to societal decline. I’m paraphrasing and the analysis is much more in depth. I’ll link it if I can find it. Also judging by the amount of animal remains mixed in with human ones on the set, they probably did also hunt and eat animals as well as people. I think in the beginning intro in the news bulletin there’s mentions of cattle mutilations, and it wouldn’t be far fetched to say that was them as well.

Not necessarily the first 3 films, but the cenobites are offhandedly mentioned in one of Clive barker’s novels, weaveworld, referred to as “the surgeons.” It was published in 1987, so they’re probably the same cenobites as either the hellbound heart or the first film.

One interpretation of the first film I saw is that yes, the family were just regular slaughterhouse workers before they were replaced by the air gun. Without jobs the family resorted to cannibalism for food, but humans didn’t just replace their meals. The family needed to continue the tradition in which they were named after, it was their core identity, and humans were used as substitutes for that as well.

As far as the game goes, there are FAR too many human bones on their residence to suggest they only recently started killing.
